problem_text:
A logistics company must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical component over a 15-week operational timeline.  
The starting stock at the warehouse at the outset of the planning window is 98 units.  
In each week \( t = 1, \dots, 15 \), the supplier permits the company to submit a procurement request whose size must fall between 18 and 80 units.  
Nevertheless, every request issued will require 4 week(s) of lead time before the components become available to meet requirements or augment the stockpile.  
The requirement for the component in each week is specified as follows:  
* Week 1: requirement 48 units  
* Week 2: requirement 16 units  
* Week 3: requirement 46 units  
* Week 4: requirement 25 units  
* Week 5: requirement 11 units  
* Week 6: requirement 12 units  
* Week 7: requirement 60 units  
* Week 8: requirement 16 units  
* Week 9: requirement 56 units  
* Week 10: requirement 29 units  
* Week 11: requirement 15 units  
* Week 12: requirement 47 units  
* Week 13: requirement 35 units  
* Week 14: requirement 55 units  
* Week 15: requirement 18 units  

Stock‑outs are tolerated, but any unsatisfied requirement is considered lost and will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the planning interval, component amounts may be treated as continuous quantities, and the aggregate volume of physical stock held at any moment must not surpass the warehouse’s maximum capacity of 98 units.  

In week 15, the permissible procurement quantity is capped at 29 units.  
In week 10, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 28 units.  

The aggregate expenditure over the planning horizon comprises three elements: the procurement expense, which amounts to 5 per unit acquired; the storage expense, which amounts to 1 per unit kept from one week to the next; and the penalty for unmet requirements, which amounts to 10 per unit of unsatisfied demand.  
The objective is to ascertain the optimal procurement quantity for each week and to monitor the consequent stock and shortage levels so as to minimize the total expenditure.
